title: Bounded Disclosure of Sealed Neural Data — conformance vectors
provenance: Derived from the release predicate in RFC-0009 §2 and the capacity rule in N5. The information bound itself (Theorem 1) is not a vector: it is a proof about channel width, and no finite set of cases could evidence it. What is pinned here is the arithmetic that enforces it and the refusal ordering an audit depends on.

valid_vectors.name: single_scalar_release
valid_vectors.note: cost is computed from what the reduction carries, never declared by the requester

valid_vectors.name: budget_spent_exactly
valid_vectors.note: spending a budget to exactly zero is a release, not a refusal

boundary_vectors.name: largest_issuable_grant
boundary_vectors.note: 64 log entries x 32 bits. RFC-0009 N5: a budget the log cannot record is refused at issue, because a ceiling the vault will not honour is not the binding one and no reader of the grant could tell

boundary_vectors.name: two_grants_jointly_overcommit
boundary_vectors.note: capacity is shared, so commitments sum; two grants that fit individually and not together are the same defect one step later

boundary_vectors.name: reissue_same_id_releases_its_own_commitment
boundary_vectors.note: replacing a grant must not double-count the budget it already held

rejection_vectors.name: budget_exhausted
rejection_vectors.note: the reconstruction attack: honest aggregates repeated are the signal returned one answer at a time, and bits are what stops it

rejection_vectors.name: thousand_probes_128_bit_grant
rejection_vectors.note: RFC-0009 U2: a refusal that depends on the window is charged, so polling device liveness is finite

rejection_vectors.name: withdrawn_outranks_every_other_reason
rejection_vectors.note: the audit must read the true cause, not whichever check ran first

rejection_vectors.name: empty_reduction
rejection_vectors.note: refused rather than released at zero cost: a free release is a free probe

rejection_vectors.name: log_full
rejection_vectors.note: releases stop when they cannot be recorded; an unrecorded disclosure is worse than a refused one
